blocked_claims.reason: No quantum advantage evidence exists in the frozen Phase 1 results.
QML reached 0/6 frozen targets in the matched comparison.
Evaluated TT/MPS configurations did not satisfy the frozen joint compression criterion.
The implemented quantity is an empirical safety potential; no formal proof was established.
blocked_claims.statement: The Lyapunov implementation provides a formal closed-loop stability guarantee.

blocked_claims.reason: Phase 1 used compact synthetic proxy environments and no production deployment.
Separate domain policy weights were used and zero-shot transfer was not tested.
blocked_claims.statement: One trained policy transfers zero-shot between driving and robotics.

blocked_claims.reason: No certification or standards-compliance claim is supported.

claims.statement: A shared computational framework was instantiated across autonomous-driving and robotics proxy domains.
INT8 was the only evaluated compression method on the Pareto frontier in both Phase 1 proxy domains under the frozen compression criterion.
Phase 1 did not demonstrate a robust 10% or greater optimizer-step efficiency improvement across all three locked seeds.
Classical PPO reached all six frozen domain-seed targets in the final matched comparison.

claims.limitation: No QML sample-efficiency, computational, quantum-speedup, or quantum-hardware advantage was demonstrated.
claims.statement: The evaluated PQC/QML actor was substantially more parameter-compact than the full PPO actor.

claims.limitation: This is empirical pilot evidence and does not establish a formal safety guarantee.
claims.statement: Explicit safety filtering reduced the observed clean violation-step rate to zero in both evaluated proxy domains.
Gaussian observation, structured-state, and direct action perturbation robustness were evaluated under the frozen Phase 1 protocol.
Explicit filtering recovered a measurable fraction of unsafe directly perturbed actions under the evaluated synthetic action-perturbation protocol.

claims.limitation: The Phase 1 evidence does not demonstrate one universal trained policy, zero-shot policy transfer, or one universal safety controller.
claims.statement: Cross-domain reuse was demonstrated at the framework, interface, evaluation, and protocol levels.

global_limitations.statement: The shared Phase 1 VLA baseline is compact and does not represent a production-scale pretrained VLA backbone.
Sprint 4 RL policies consume compact environment state rather than the Sprint 1 shared VLA latent representation.
The principal trained-policy protocol uses three seeds.
Safety evaluations use 20 held-out episodes per seed/condition in the principal protocol.
The Phase 1 hybrid QML pathway uses a small simulated 4-qubit, 2-layer PQC.
No quantum hardware execution was performed.
TT/MPS compression was evaluated at pilot-model scale.
No principal CARLA, nuScenes, or physical-vehicle evaluation was performed.
No principal RLBench, LIBERO, Open X-Embodiment, or physical-robot evaluation was performed.
During perception-perturbation experiments, the policy used perturbed/noisy observations while the safety layer retained access to true simulator state.
Environment action-bound handling is accounted for separately from explicit safety-filter intervention.
The implemented Lyapunov quantity is an empirical safety potential and does not constitute a formal closed-loop stability proof.
No functional-safety certification or standards compliance is claimed.
No production deployment or full-scale embedded VLA validation was performed.

architecture.allowed_summary: Cross-domain reuse is supported at the framework and interface level, not as one universal trained policy.

compression.allowed_summary: INT8 remained the strongest Phase 1 compression result; TT/MPS provided an implemented quantum-inspired pathway without demonstrating superiority.

rl_qml.allowed_summary: Classical PPO reached all frozen targets. The hybrid PQC actor was substantially more compact but did not demonstrate sample-efficiency advantage.

safety.allowed_summary: Explicit safety filtering produced strong empirical pilot effects. Robustness was evaluated across Gaussian, structured-state, and action perturbations. Lyapunov-specific mechanism activation remained domain-dependent.

training_efficiency.allowed_summary: No robust >=10% training-efficiency improvement was demonstrated under the frozen Phase 1 protocol.
